name: Jadon
overview: Jadon is a male figure identified as the Meronothite who played a practical role in the restoration efforts recorded in Nehemiah. His unique contribution was making repairs to the official seat of the governor, highlighting his involvement in the physical rebuilding of Jerusalem's infrastructure. Beyond this, Scripture provides no further personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jadon means either 'frail one' or 'YHWH rules,' reflecting Hebrew linguistic roots. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God, but it carries significant theological resonance through its possible meanings.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Jadon beyond what is noted in his unique attribute as the Meronothite involved in repair work. No additional relational information is provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jadon's significance lies in his contribution to the rebuilding of Jerusalem during the post-exilic period, specifically through repairing the governor's official seat. This task underscores the communal effort led by Nehemiah to restore the city's governance and worship centers. Though a minor figure, his work reflects the faithful service essential to the restoration of God's people and their city.
